name: Step-3.7-Flash

sources.note: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable

purpose: StepFun states: a 198B vision-language MoE for high-frequency production workloads, built for developers who scale agentic workflows combining perception, search and reasoning (financial report parsing, multi-step search loops, concurrent coding agents).

license.name: Apache-2.0 (card tag; no LICENSE file in the repository)
license.notes: Card YAML says apache-2.0; neither the main repo nor the official GGUF repo has a LICENSE file, so the text could not be read.

architecture.gguf_arch: step3p5 (name from config.json; llama.cpp support stated by the vendor)
architecture.attention: full attention every fourth layer, sliding window 512 on the others (layer_types in config.json)
architecture.drafter: MTP head (3 layers; separate GGUF 3.7 to 7.0 GB in the official repo)
architecture.why_this_design: The card states the target (throughput up to 400 tok/s, three selectable reasoning levels, 256k context) but no reasons for the attention layout.

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from the file size (75.8 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 60 GB; about 13% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-16gb.notes: estimate from the file size (75.8 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 64 GB; about 18% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (75.8 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 21.6 GB VRAM plus 82 GB RAM = 104 GB; about 28% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (75.8 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 29.6 GB VRAM plus 114 GB RAM = 144 GB; about 39% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

mac-16-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (75.8 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 12 GB)

mac-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (75.8 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 22 GB)

engine_support.notes: Official GGUFs; a llama.cpp reasoning-parser bug was being fixed in July 2026 (PR 25238 per HF discussion 14). Tona would need a new module (step3p5: SWA-512 + full layers, MoE).

benchmarks.name: AA Coding Index (aggregator mirror)
benchmarks.harness: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable

benchmarks.name: AA Intelligence Index
benchmarks.harness: from a search result snippet; the same snippet gives 57 for GLM-5.3-Flash; page not fetched (404 for us)

strengths: Official GGUFs and MTP; Apache-2.0 by card
Strong vendor SWE-bench Pro 56.3 and ClawEval
weaknesses: Independent Coding Index 39.6 is well below the vendor picture and below Ling 3.0 Flash (50.6)
Thinks long: stuck-in-thinking loops reported (one user burned 40 M tokens in Kilo Code), no off switch in the stock template
Raw tool-call tokens leaking into output during long exploration (HF discussion 12)
soft.behavior: Three reasoning levels; the stock chat template always opens a think block (community patch for enable_thinking).
best_for: agentic workflows with vision input on large-memory machines
soft.maturity: StepFun: Step 3.5 and 3.7 releases; 9.6k downloads of the main repo, 16 discussions.

user_reports.summary: Thinking loop in Kilo Code burned 40 M tokens (vLLM, MTP at 3)
Raw tool-call tokens appear mid-reasoning during long codebase exploration (pi harness, official API)
On a 5090 + RTX PRO 6000 at Q4_K_S it thinks 5 to 60 s per turn, slower than Step 3.5 Flash (3 to 10 s)

tona_fit.reason: Official GGUFs and a clean Apache-2.0 tag, but the only independent coding number (39.6) is the lowest of the Flash class, thinking behaviour is reported as slow and loop-prone, and the smallest quant (76 GB) reaches only the 32 GB + 128 GB class and the 24 GB + 96 GB class marginally.
blockers: Tona has no step3p5 module (engine support, not a quality judgement)

open_questions: Why the independent Coding Index (39.6) is far below the vendor SWE-bench Pro 56.3: index version or harness? Check: AA methodology page and our own SWE subset.

Per-language coding quality: no public per-language numbers found (vendor tables are aggregates; swebench.com per-language view not retrievable). Check: run our Exercism polyglot set per language on the model.
